questions.testName: 2024 December GENERAL Paper-I Shift-I
questions.questionText: When 20% of a number (x) is added to another number (y), the number (y) increases by 50%. What is the respective ratio between the two numbers x and y?
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : Adding 20% of \(x\) to \(y\) increases by 50%.

\[
20\%=\frac{20}{100}=\frac{1}{5}
\]

An increase of 50% means:

\[
\frac{50}{100}+1=\frac{3}{2}=1.5
\]

\[
y+\frac{1}{5}x=y+\frac{50}{100}y
\]

\[
y+\frac{1}{5}x=\frac{3}{2}y
\]

Subtract \(y\) from both sides:

\[
\frac{1}{5}x=\frac{3}{2}y-y
\]

\[
\frac{1}{5}x=\frac{3}{2}y-\frac{2}{2}y
\]

\[
\frac{1}{5}x=\frac{1}{2}y
\]

\[
\frac{x}{y}=\frac{5}{2}
\]

\[
x:y=5:2
\]

38. Four persons A, B, C and D play a game of
cards. A says to B. "If I give you 8 cards you
will have as many as C has and I shall have 3
less than what C has. Also, if I take 6 cards
from C. I shall have twice as many as D has". If
B and D together have 50 cards, how many
cards has A got?
questions.explanation:
Ans. (d) : If A gives & cards to B then B will have as
many as C has and A will have 3 less than what C has
\(\to  B+8 = C ...(i)\)
\(= A–8 = C–3\)
\(= C = A – 5 ... (ii)\)
• Also if A takes 6 cards from C, a will have twice as
many as D has.
\(\to  A + 6 = 2D ... (iii)\)
• B and D together have
\(\to  B +D = 50 or D = 50–B ... (iv)\)
Now putting (ii) into (i), we have
\(\to  B+8 = A–5\)
\(A–B = 13 ... (v)\)
\(A = 13+B ... (a)\)
Putting (iv) into (iii), we have
\(\to  A+6 = 2(50–B)\)
\(= A+6 = 100–2B\)
\(= A+2B = 94 ... (vi)\)
\(\to  A = 94–2B ... (b)\)
Solving (a) and (b) we get–
\(13+B = 94–2B\)
\(3B = 94–13\)
\(3B = 81\)
\(B = 27\)
Putting value of (b) in (a) we get–
\(A = 13+27\)
\(A = 40\)

Ayurveda defines health as a dynamic balance
of the internal environment that positively
influences the sensory organs, mind and self.
Every individual is unique and has a unique
mental and physical makeup that determines
his vulnerability to disease and his opportunity
to achieve a high level of health. Ayurveda has
been a pioneer in advocating individualized
medicine since historical times. Advances in
human genetics and medicinal genetics have
today led to the emergence of an individualized
approach to medicine that tailors medical
intervention to individual needs.
Ayurveda indicates that maintaining the
balance of the internal environment requires
harmony with the external environment.
Ayurveda declares that man is a representative
of the universe, a miniature replica of the vast
universe and man is made up of the same
elements that make up nature. Thus Ayurveda
evolved as an eco-conscious system of health
care. For people living in a particular place, the
plants growing around them are most suitable.
Every person has to carve out a lifestyle for
himself which takes into account the
geographical area and the changing seasons.

Handicraft is the processing of goods/materials

Read the following passage and answer the
question:
Every now and then some retired civil servants come
out with his memoirs, painting a glorious picture of the
heights of administrative efficiency reached during his
reign. There is often the suggestion that had there not
been so much political interference, things would have
been even more fantastic. It is not unusual for the self-
styled hero to blame not only interfering politicians but
also fellow civil servants who were idiots or crooks, for
his failures. This attitude of smug satisfaction is,
unfortunately developed during the years of service. Self
preservation rather than service is encouraged by our
whole system of rules and procedures.
The remedy has to be drastic and quickly effective.
the over protection now granted to civil servants must
end. Today to remove an erring civil servant is just not
possible. And the only thing that the highest authority in
the Government, both in the state and at the centre, can
do is to transfer an official from one job to another.
The rules for taking disciplinary action are so
complicated that, in the end, defaulting civil servant gets
away, and gets his full emoluments even for the period of
the disciplinary proceedings, thus making it a paid
holiday for him.
The result is that the administration has become
rule-oriented and not result oriented. Action is possible
against the official who takes some interest in his work,
but no action is ever taken against a person who does not
deliver the goods. If the country is to adopt a result
oriented approach, it is necessary to link job performance
with job retention.

16. Which of the following is an example of
deductive reasoning?
questions.optionA:
Screen exposure among children at very early
stage affects their Psychological health.
Therefore, we should not expose our children
to digital gadgets.
questions.optionB:
Smoking leads to lung cancer. Therefore, we
should not smoke.
questions.optionC:
If it is raining, then the ground is wet. It is
raining. Therefore, the ground is wet.
questions.optionD:
All ducks that have been observed have been
white. Therefore all ducks are white.
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : The following is an example of deductive
reasoning :
Premise 1 – If P, then Q (If it is raining, then the
ground is wet).
Premise 2 – Specific instance (It is raining)
Conclusion – Therefore, Q (Therefore, the ground is
wet).
This fits the definition of deductive reasoning perfectly.
If both premises are true, the conclusion must be true.

The stock-taking done at the first national

Comprehension :
Read the following passage and answer the

A person who takes the trouble to form his own
opinions and beliefs, will feel that he owes no
responsibility to the majority for his conclusions. If he is
a genuine lover of truth, if he is inspired by a passion for
seeing things as they are and an abhorrence of holding
ideas which do not conform to facts, he will be wholly
independent of the assent of those around him. When he
proceeds to apply his beliefs in the practical conduct of
life, the position is different. There are then good reasons
why his attitude should be less inflexible. The society in
which he is placed is an ancient and composite growth.
The people from whom he dissents have not come by
their opinions, customs and by a process of mere
haphazard.
These opinions and customs all had their origin in a
certain real supposed fitness. They have certain depth of
root in the lives of a proportion of the existing
generation. Their congruity with one another may have
come to an end. That is only one side of the truth. The
most zealous propagandism cannot penetrate to them. In
common language, we speak of a generation as
something possessed of a kind of exact unity, with all its
parts and members homogenous. Yet, plainly it is not
this. It is a whole but a whole in a state of constant flux,
its factors and elements are eternally shifting. It is not
one but many generations.

obvious that someday, the human race will disappear

informal fallacy where one assumes that a characteristic

is smoke." is fallacious according to classical Indian
school of logic (Nyaya) because it is based on

smoke, for example dry fuel. The fallacy lies in
mistaking a conditional relationship for an

observed, cannot be explained without assuming

perception of inconsistency.

questions.questionText:
6. Which of the following statements contradict
each other?
A. All ducks are birds.
B. Some ducks are birds.
C. Some ducks are not birds.
D. No ducks are birds.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : On logical analysis of the statements referred
to in the question -
(A) All ducks are birds, means every duck is a bird.
(B) Some ducks are birds, means at least one duck is
bird. This is the generalization of A, not the
contradiction. If A is true then B will also be true.
(C) All ducks are not birds, means there is at least one
duck which is not a bird. This contradicts statements
A.
(D) No duck is a bird, means not a single duck is a bird.
This contradicts both A and B.
It is clear from the above analysis that statements (B)
and (D) contradict each other. Both of them cannot be
true at the same time, because B claims that at least
some ducks are birds and D contradicts it. It is
significant that contradiction means that two statements
cannot be true and false at the same time.

questions.questionText:
7. Why is the concentration of CO2 is more in the
Northern Hemisphere than the Southern
Hemisphere?
A. Land mass is more in the Northern
Hemisphere.
B. Ocean body is more in the Southern
Hemisphere
C. Fossil fuel is burnt more in the Northern
Hemisphere
D. Northern Hemisphere is colder than the
Southern Hemisphere
Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : The concentration of CO2 is higher in the
Northern Hemisphere mainly because it has more land
mass leading to greater human activity and emissions,
and because fossil fuel is burnt more in the Northern
Hemisphere. The Southern Hemisphere, with more
ocean, absorbs more CO2, reducing its atmospheric
concentration. Therefore,
(A) 'Land mass is more in the Northern Hemisphere' is
correct because larger land mass means more
industrialization, human activities and CO2 Sources.
(B) 'Ocean body is more in the Southern Hemisphere' is
correct because oceans act as major CO2 sinks,
absorbing more CO2 and lowering atmospheric
levels in the south.
(C) 'Fossil fuel is burnt more in the Northern
Hemisphere is correct because most industrialized
nations (CO2 producers) are located in the Northern
Hemisphere.
(D) 'Northern Hemisphere is colder than the Southern
Hemisphere' is not a major factor because there is
no evidence that colder climate in the Northern
Hemisphere directly causes higher CO2
concentration.
Hence, option (c) is correct.

13. According to the classical Indian School of
logic, which of the following instruments of
knowledge is defined as the knowledge of the
relation between a word and its…………..
produced by the knowledge of resemblance or
similarity?
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : In the classical Indian School of logic,
particularly in the Nyaya System, Upamana
(Comparison) is defined as the instrument of knowledge
that arises from understanding the relation between a
word and its denotation through resemblance or
similarity. For example, if someone, has never seen an
animal called 'gavaya' (wild cow) before, and is told
that 'gavaya' looks like a cow, he acquires knowledge
about 'gavaya' based on the similarity between 'cow' and
'gavaya'. He mentally forms an image of 'gavaya' based
on the characteristics of cow (such as size, four legs,
horns etc). This is a method of acquiring knowledge
through analogy, where the properties of an already
known object (cow) are applied to an unkown object
(gavaya).

therefore Mr. X who is a member of this
fraternity must be one of the richest young man
on the campus." Which fallacy us involved in
this argument?
questions.explanation:
Ans. (a) : The argument referred to in the question
argues on the basis that if a group (fraternity group) is
prosperous, then each of its members (Mr. X) must also
be prosperous. This is a fallacy of division, because the
characteristic of the group (prosperity) cannot be
automatically applied to each of its members. The
prosperity of the fraternity group may be due to the
wealth or other factors of some members, and Mr. X
may not be prosperous individually.

27. Arrange the following in order of increasing
extension.
A. Social Science
B. Political Science
C. Sciences
D. Politics of International Relations
Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.explanation:
Ans. (d) : Scope means which subject is the broadest
and which is the narrowest. Science is the broadest
subject as it includes natural sciences like Physics,
Chemistry, Biology which deal with tangible,
measurable physical phenomena. Social science studies
human society and social relations, so it is less broad
than science. Political Science is a subfield of social
science which studies political systems and behaviour.
Politics of international relations is another specialized
field of political science which focuses on political
relations between nations. So, on arranging the subjects
in the increasing order of their scope, we get the
following order-
Politics of International Relations → Political Science
→ Social Science → Science

intestinal tract

fecal contamination

Ans. (d) : The following statements about coliform
bacteria are true -
(A) Coliform bacteria are used in testing water
contamination. These bacteria are used as indicators
to check water quality, especially to detect faecal
contamination.
(B) The statement that coliform bacteria are harmless
and do not cause disease is partly true because most
coliform bacteria are not actually pathogenic,
although they are indicators of the presence of

strains of Esherichia coli (E. coli), can cause
disease.
(C) Coliform bacteria are naturally found in the
intestines of humans and other warm-blooded
animals.
(D) The presence of coliform in water is indicator of
faecal contamination.
Hence, option (d) is correct.

43. If the statement "No birds are animals" is
given as false, which of the following statements
can be inferred to be true?
A. Some animals are not birds.
B. Some ducks are birds.
C. Some animals are birds.
D. Some birds are animals.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.optionD: A, B, C and D Only
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : If the statement 'No birds are animals' is
taken to be false then statement (c) and statement (d)
can be inferred to be true because :
* Statement 'Some animals are birds' is equivalent to
'Some birds are animals' and is a valid inference.
* Statement 'Some birds are animals' is the direct
negation of the original statement and is the most
direct and accurate inference.
Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.questionText: 44. What is Explanatory research?
questions.optionA:
It studies subject about which either no
information or the limited information is
available.
questions.optionB:
It describes social situations, social events,
social systems, social structures etc. The
researcher observes/studies and then
describes what did he find?
questions.optionC:
It explains the causes of social phenomena.
Describing the magnitude and nature of
crimes committed by females in India is one
aspect of female crime but why do they
commit crime is its explanatory aspect.
questions.optionD:
It is based on common sense knowledge
based on the accumulated experiences and
beliefs of the people.
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : Explanatory research explains the causes of
social phenomena. Describing the magnitude and nature
of crimes committed by females in India is one aspect
of female crime but why do they commit crime is its
explanatory aspect. Through this research, emphasis is
laid on presenting the events or facts in the same form
as they actually are. In this type of research design, facts
or material are collected through questionnaire,
interview schedule and observation etc. Also, the event
is mentioned in it, on the basis of which the reality is
studied. This research is adopted to know the
characteristics of a situation, group or a particular
person.

questions.questionText: 45. What is Exploratory Research?
questions.optionA:
It describes social situations, social events,
social systems, social structures etc. The
researcher observes/studies and then
describes what did he find?
questions.optionB:
It studies subject about which either no
information or the limited information is
available.
questions.optionC:
It explains the causes of social phenomena.
Describing the magnitude and nature of
crimes committed by females in India is one
aspect of female crime but why do they
commit crime is its explanatory aspect.
questions.optionD:
It is based on common sense knowledge
based on the accumulated experiences and
beliefs of the people.
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : Exploratory Research studies subject about
which either no information or the limited information
is available. It helps to provide new insights and set the
direction for future research. Exploratory research is
concerned with the discovery of new facts. Exploratory
research design is used to study already existing facts
or theories in detail. Its goal is to gain in-depth in sight
into a paricular subject.

Forced by circumstances and in pursuit of success

questions.questionText: 8. What is not a Research?
questions.optionA:
Research is a careful and exhaustive
investigation of a phenomenon with an
objective of advancing knowledge.
questions.optionB:
It is a systematic and objective attempt to
study a problem for the purpose of deriving
general principles.
questions.optionC:
Research is based on common sense
knowledge, based on the accumulated
experiences and beliefs of the people.
questions.optionD:
It is a systematic investigation to find
solutions to a problem.
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : Research is an activity that leads us to finding
new facts, information, assisting us in verifying the
available knowledge and in making us question things
that are difficult to understand as per existing data.

accumulated experiences, or beliefs. Instead, it involves
systematic, objective and evidence– based investigation
to advance knowledge or solve problems, as described
in options 1, 2 and 4.

includes encryption, providing end-to-end security
for data transmission.
(E) A Trojan is a type of malware that disguises itself as
legitimate software, it is not an antivirus.

questions.questionText:
16. In the Buddha Period, which educational
centres were established along with monasteries?
A. BAllabhi B. Baba Mastnath University
C. Nalanada D. Vikramshila
E. Taxila
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionB: A, B, C and D Only
questions.optionC: A, C, D and E Only
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : The most notable centres of learning in India
during the Buddha Period were :
(i) Taxila : Taxila was a significant location for the
dissemination of brahmanical knowledge. Even
throughout the time of the Buddhists, its reputation
remained strong in Northern India. Taxila gave birth to
both Panini, who is considered to be the Father of
'Vyakarana', and Jivaka, who was an expert in both
surgery and medicine. Taxila was the location where the
famous Indian author kautilya, who is most known for
writing the ''Asthashastra'' completed his academic
education.
(ii) Nalanda : Nalanda was a well-known cultural and
educational centre in Northern India. It was located
forty miles south-west of modern Patna and seven miles
north of Rajagriha. Nalanda enjoyed a large degree of
status and importance for Buddhist monks as a result of
the fact that it was the birth place of Sariputta, a
preferred student of Lord Buddha. From the year 450
AD. during the rule of Gupta dynasty, the actual
importance of Nalanda began, and it remained at the
height of its reputation and splendour for the next three
centuries. Nalanda was the centre of Mahayana
Buddhism.
(iii) Vikramshila : King Dharmapala had built the
vihara of Vikramshila on a hillside near Nalanda in
Magadha in the 8th
century A.D.
(iv) Vallabhi : During the time of the Buddha, another
significant educational centre that flourished was
Vallabhi. It was established in 475 AD and lasted untill
775 AD. It was also a centre for Hinayana Buddhism.
By the first century, AD; Vallabhi has established a
name for itself as a centre for higher study.

questions.questionText:
29. Criteria for Hypotheses construction are
A. It should describe one issue only.
B. It should describe many issues.
C. It should specify variables between which
the relationship is to be established.
D. It should be specific and precise.
E. It should be empirically testable, whether it
is right or wrong.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.optionC: A, C, D and E Only
questions.optionD: A, B, C and D Only
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : To construct a good hypothesis, the following
criteria are essential :
(i) A hypothesis should focus on a single issue or
relationship to ensure clarity and avoid confusion.
(ii) A hypothesis must clearly identify the independent
and dependent variables and the relationship
between them.
(iii) A hypothesis should be clear, concise, and
unambiguous to guide research effectively.
(iv) A hypothesis must be testable through observation
or experimentation to determine its validity,
whether it is right or wrong.
Criteria, ''It should describe many issues'' is incorrect
because a hypothesis should focus on a single issue, not
multiple issues, to maintain clarity and testability.

33. “The world is an effect and hence it must have
an efficient and intelligent cause. That efficient
and intelligent cause is God.” Which means of
knowledge is used in this argument as per
classical Indian School of Logic (Nyāya)?
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : The argument ''The world is an effect and
hence it must have an efficient and intelligent cause.
That efficient and intelligent God,'' uses inference
(anumana) as its means of knowledge according to the
Nyaya school of classical Indian logic. Inference, in the
Nyaya system, is reasoning from observed effects to
unseen causes, or from known causes to their effects.
Here, the reasoning goes from the observed effect (the
world) to infer an unobserved cause (God).

41. Which of the following propositions are so
related that they cannot both be false, though
they can both be true?
A. Some poems are artworks.
B. All poems are artworks.
C. Some poems are not artworks.
D. Some artworks are poems.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : Propositions A and C (Some poems are
artworks and Some poems are not artworks) are sub
contrary propositions i.e. they cannot both be false
simultaneously, but they can both be true.
For instance, if the set of poems contains both artworks
and non-artworks, both statements would be true.
However, if one is false, the other must be true. If
''some poems are not artworks'' is false, it means ''All
poems are artworks'' is true, which makes ''Some poems
are artworks'' true.

Comprehension :
Read the following passage and answer the questions
that follow :
What do you think is scary? A Halloween spook
house? A haunted com maze? A slasher movie?
Certainly these kinds of things can give you a shiver, but
- really - don't we all know they are just make-believe,
acknowledged fictions? In real life, what is more likely
to be really scary are things like finding your keys locked
in the car, or discovering termites in the foundation of
your home, or hearing the telephone ringing in the
middle of the night.
Urban legends (ULs) are scary when they combine
horror fiction with the details of real life. In typical ULs
you encounter shocks such as lurking criminals,
threatening maniacs, vague unknown dangers, faulty
products and isolated victims, all set in the context of
everyday life. Such stories are told by a friend as
something that happened to his or her close acquaintance
(a friend of a friend, or a FOAF). Urban legends are
packed with local details and related with an air of
conviction. While these stories are not literally true, any
more than a horror film is, when hearing them we realize
that they could be true!

questions.questionText: 6. Which of the following is correct?
questions.optionA:
Factor design is used for one dependent
variable and two or more independent
variables
questions.optionB: Factor design is used for extraneous variables
questions.optionC:
Factor design has only one independent
variable
questions.optionD:
Factor design is used for two on more
dependent variables
questions.explanation:
Ans. (a) : A factor design (often called a factorial
design) is an experimental setup that looks at the effects
of two or more independent variables—known as
factors—on a single dependent variable.
Factor design is used for one dependent variable and
two or more independent variables.
This is true. Factor designs (especially factorial
experiments) are commonly used in research when there
is one dependent variable and at least two independent
variables (factors) that researchers want to investigate
simultaneously.
Factor design is used for extraneous variables.
This is false. Factor design is not specifically aimed at
handling extraneous variables. Extraneous variables are
typically addressed through experimental controls or
randomization.
Factor design has only one independent variable.
This is false. By definition, factor designs involve more
than one independent variable, as they explore the
interaction between factors.
Factor design is used for two or more dependent
variables.
This is false. Factor design focuses on how multiple
independent variables affect a single dependent
variable, not multiple dependent variables.
The correct answer is Option 1: Factor design is used
for one dependent variable and two or more
independent variables. If you'd like, I can explain more
about factorial experiments or other research designs!
Advantages of Factor Design
• Efficiency: Because all combinations of factors are
tested, factorial designs provide more information
per experiment compared to conducting several
separate experiments.
• Insight into Interactions: They allow researchers to
observe whether factors interact, providing a deeper
understanding of the underlying processes affecting
the dependent variable.
• Generalizability: By testing multiple variables
simultaneously, factorial designs can often better
mirror real-world situations where multiple factors
are at play.

questions.questionText:
9. ''There is no theoretical principle that can not
be put into practice because such theoretical
principle is no theoretical principle at all''
Which logical fallacy is committed in the above
argument?
questions.explanation:
Ans. (d) : The argument states: "There is no
theoretical principle that cannot be put into practice
because such theoretical principle is no theoretical
principle at all."
This statement is circular in its reasoning. It essentially
assumes what it needs to prove: that every theoretical
principle must be capable of being put into practice. In
doing so, it uses its own conclusion as part of its
justification. Here's a breakdown:
Circular Reasoning: The argument presupposes that if
a theoretical principle cannot be turned into practice, it
loses its status as a "theoretical principle." By defining a
theoretical principle in terms of its practical
applicability, it assumes the very point it's trying to
establish.
Begging the Question: This is the textbook example of
"begging the question" or circular argumentation. It
doesn't provide external evidence or logical steps
independent of its conclusion; instead, it just reaffirms
the conclusion within the premise.
In contrast, the other options represent different logical
fallacies:
Slippery Slope: Involves arguing that a minor action
will lead to major and oftentimes ludicrous
consequences.
Straw Man: Involves misrepresenting an opponent's
argument to make it easier to attack.
Inappropriate Authority: Involves citing an authority
who is not actually qualified to speak on the subject.
Since none of these describe the reasoning used in the
argument, the fallacy committed here is indeed begging
the question.

questions.questionText:
10. Which of the following statements are so
related that they cannot both be true, nor can
they both be false?
A. All dogs are omnivores
B. Some dogs are omnivores
C. Some dogs are not omnivores
D. No dogs are omnivorcs
Choose the correct answer from the
options given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (a) : Logical Relationship: Statement A and
Statement C are exact logical opposites—one is the
negation of the other.
• If A is true (all dogs are omnivores), then C must be
false (there cannot be a dog that is not omnivorous).
• If A is false (not all dogs are omnivores), then the
exact negation is that at least one dog is not an
omnivore, which makes C true.
Thus, A and C can never be both true or both false.
Other Options
Pair B and C:
• B (―Some dogs are omnivores‖) and C (―Some dogs
are not omnivores‖) can both be true in a mixed
scenario where some dogs are omnivores and some
are not. Hence, they don’t have the required
property.
Pair C and D:
• D (―No dogs are omnivores‖) implies that every dog
is non-omnivorous, so C (―Some dogs are not
omnivores‖) would be true automatically. However,
if all dogs are omnivores then both would be false.
So they can in fact be simultaneously false.
Pair A and D:
• A (―All dogs are omnivores‖) and D (―No dogs are
omnivores‖) clearly cannot both be true. But if the
truth is that the dog population is mixed (some
omnivores and some non-omnivores), then A is
false (not all dogs are omnivores) and D is also false
(since some dogs are omnivores). Thus, A and D
can both be false, which does not meet the
condition.
Only Pair A and C have the property that they cannot
both be true and cannot both be false—they always
have opposite truth values.
Thus, the correct answer is: 1. A and C only.

11. Arrange the following developments in mass
communication in chronological sequence.
A. Invention of Printing Press
B. Launch of first Television network
C. Emergence of ratio broadcasting
D. Creation of the internet
E. Introduction of social media platforms
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (d) : identifying the historical timeline for each
development:
1. Invention of Printing Press (A): This occurred in
the mid-15th century (around 1440, with Johannes
Gutenberg).
2. Emergence of Radio Broadcasting (C): Radio
broadcasting began in the early 20th century (the 1920s
saw its rapid development).
3. Launch of First Television Network (B): Although
experimental television existed earlier, the first
dedicated television network started regular broadcasts
in the 1930s (for instance, the BBC began its television
service in 1936).
4. Creation of the Internet (D): The foundations for
the internet (ARPANET) began in the late 1960s,
leading to its broader development by the late 20th
century.
5. Introduction of Social Media Platforms (E): Social
media as we recognize it emerged in the 21st century
(with platforms such as Facebook starting in the mid-
2000s).
Given these historical milestones, the chronological
sequence is:
A (Printing Press) → C (Radio Broadcasting) → B
(Television Network) → D (Internet) → E (Social
Media Platforms).
Thus, the correct option is:
Option 4: A, C, B, D, E.

designed to help users perform specific tasks. Here's a
breakdown of each option:
Internet Explorer (A) & Mozilla Firefox (B): These

of application software, as it allows users to access and
interact with web content.
Microsoft Office (C) & Apache Open Office (D):
These are office suites that include word processors,
spreadsheet programs, and presentation software. They
are intended for productivity and document creation,
making them application software.

considered system software because it manages
hardware and provides a platform for running
application programs, rather than being an application
itself.
Thus, only options A, B, C, and D are examples of
application software.

called_____. A page orientation can be either
_______ or ______. The special margin that is
placed at the top or edge to clear the text from
the fold in a page is called the_______. When
the first line of a paragraph appears in the last
line of a page, then this is called_______.
A. Portrait
B. Gutter
C. Point
D. Orphan
E. Landscape
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : each blank with the appropriate term:
1. Font Size Unit: The unit used to measure the size of
a font is point. → C
2. Page Orientation: A page orientation can be either
portrait or landscape. → The natural order is ―portrait‖
first and then ―landscape.‖ That gives:
• First blank: Portrait (A)
• Second blank: Landscape (E)
3. Special Margin: The margin that is specially added
to clear the text from the fold in a page is called the
gutter. → B

appears alone at the bottom of a page, it is called an
orphan. → D
Thus, placing the letters in order corresponding to each

questions.questionText:
18. Identify the correct statements regarding
variables.
A. The researcher manipulates an
independent variable
B. A dependent variable is the outcome being
measured
C. Extraneous variables are always controlled
D. Control variables lead to spurious
relationships
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (a) : Statements:
A. The researcher manipulates an independent
variable. Explanation: Yes, in experimental research,
the researcher deliberately manipulates the independent
variable to observe its effect on the dependent variable.
B. A dependent variable is the outcome being
measured. Explanation: Yes, the dependent variable
represents the outcome that is measured in response to
changes in the independent variable.
C. Extraneous variables are always controlled.
Explanation: This statement is not entirely correct.
Extraneous variables are potential confounders that
could influence the dependent variable. Researchers try
to control or account for them, but it is not always
possible to control all extraneous variables in every
study.
D. Control variables lead to spurious relationships.
Explanation: This statement is incorrect. Control
variables are used to minimize the impact of extraneous
factors, not to create spurious (false) relationships. In
fact, control variables are included to isolate the
relationship between the independent and the dependent
variables, thereby reducing the chance of spurious
correlations.
The correct answer is Option 1: A and B only.

indicates its clock speed. The clock speed represents the
number of cycles the CPU can perform per second. For
instance, a CPU with a clock speed of 3 GHz means it
can complete 3 billion cycles each second. This
measurement directly reflects the processing speed and
overall performance of the CPU.

access times, not in Hertz.

23. Which of the following statements are true
regarding Takshshila?
A. The great grammarian Panini had his
education there.
B. Kautilya was a learner there

education

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (d) : Statement A: "The great grammarian Panini
received his education there." Historical tradition holds
that Panini, the renowned Sanskrit grammarian famous
for his work Ashtadhyayi, was associated with
Takshashila. This makes Statement A true.
Statement B: "Kautilya was a student there." Kautilya
(also known as Chanakya) is historically known to have
studied at Takshashila, where he later became a key
figure in the establishment of the Maurya Empire.
Therefore, Statement B is also true.
Statement D: "Students had to pay for their education."
This statement is incorrect because, contrary to the idea
of charging fees, ancient Takshashila was known for

questions.questionText:
25. According to classical Indian logicians
(Naiyayikas), which of the following arguments
has an irregular middle term defect?
questions.optionA: Sound is a quality because it is visible.
questions.optionB: Sound is eternal because it is produced.
questions.optionC: Sound is eternal because it is audible.
questions.optionD: Fire is cold because it is a substance.
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : Option 3. In the Nyāya system of logic, an
inference (anumāna) is constructed with a middle term
that links the subject to the predicate through a reason
(hetu). For a syllogism to be valid, the middle term must
exhibit a proper and universal concomitance (vyāpti)
between the two premises.
An irregular (or non-uniform) middle term occurs when
the quality or property used as the reason in the
inference is not consistently or appropriately distributed
between the subject and the predicate, thereby failing to
establish the necessary logical connection.
Let’s briefly examine the options:
1. Option 1: ―Sound is a quality because it is matter.‖ –
Here, the middle term is ―matter‖ (õJÙe). In classical
Indian thought, qualities (]iegCe) are considered to inhere
in matter. Although the argument is debatable on other
grounds, the linking property ―matter‖ is intended to be
a regular medium for attributing qualities. (It does not
illustrate the specific flaw of an irregular middle term.)
2. Option 2: ―Sound is eternal because it is produced.‖
– In this inference, the reason is ―being produced.‖ This
claim raises its own issues—namely, production implies
a beginning, so it is a suspect basis for declaring
eternality—but it primarily falls into a different kind of
error rather than that of an irregular middle term.
3. Option 3: ―Sound is eternal because it is audible.‖ –
In this argument, the property used as the middle term is
―audibility‖ (ßeJÙelee). Classical Nyāya insists that the
middle term (here, ―audible‖) must universally connect
the reason and the predicate. However, audibility does
not have a necessary or invariable connection with
eternality. The mere fact that something is heard does
not serve as a proper basis to infer that it is eternal. This
irregularity in the distribution of the middle term (i.e.,
―audibility‖ does not carry the concomitant of eternality
throughout its domain) is what makes this syllogism
fallacious under Nyāya criticism. Thus, Option 3 is the
argument that exhibits an irregular middle term.
4. Option 4: ―Fire is cold because it is matter.‖ –
Although this argument is clearly unsound (fire is not
cold and being matter is not a reason to attribute
coldness), the error here is not specifically about an
irregular middle term but rather an inappropriate or
false connection between the properties.
According to classical Nyāya logic, the argument that
commits the error of an irregular middle term is:
(Sound is eternal because it is audible.)
Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.

26. Which of the following are the characteristics
of learner-centred assessment strategies?
questions.optionB:
It involves skills depending on the needs of
the learners.
questions.optionC:
It involves individual and collaborative
elements.
questions.optionD:
It is related to the learning goals of the
students.
(E) Learners are passively involved in the
assessment process.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
(a) Only A, C, D and E
(b) Only C and D
(c) Only B, D and E
(d) Only A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
Ans. (d) : Option 1: Only A, B, C, and D
Student‐centered assessment strategies are designed to
focus on the learning process and individual growth of
the student. Their key characteristics typically include:
1. Multiple Sources of Data (Statement A):
Student‐centered assessment does not rely on a single
test or measure; instead, it gathers evidence from
various sources (such as projects, observations, self-
assessments, portfolios, etc.). This diversity in data
collection helps in getting a well-rounded picture of a
student’s learning.
2. Practical and Collaborative Elements (Statement
C): Such strategies often include tasks that are
authentic, practical, and require collaboration. This
approach helps learners to apply their knowledge in
real-life contexts and learn from peers, which is a
hallmark of a student-centered environment.
3. Addressing Learners’ Learning Difficulties
(Statement D): A formative, student-centered
assessment is diagnostic by nature. It seeks to identify
and address the issues or misconceptions that learners
face in their learning process so that targeted support
can be provided.
While the idea of ―taking into account the needs of the
learners‖ (Statement B) is important in instructional
design, when it comes to characterizing assessment
strategies that are truly student-centered, the emphasis is
placed on how the assessment is carried out—using
multiple data sources, practical and collaborative tasks,
diagnostic feedback, and active learner involvement. In
many models of student-centered assessment, the focus
shifts from a teacher-driven determination of needs to a
process where students actively engage in and take
responsibility for their learning. Thus, although
Statement B is attractive in principle, the core attributes
(as recognized in this question) concentrate on the
features listed in A, B, C, and D.
Based on the above analysis, the characteristics of
student-centered assessment strategies are best
described by statements A, C, D, and E.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1: Only A, B, C
and D.

In 1925, an organization was established in India with
the aim of promoting university activities by facilitating
the sharing of information and cooperation in the fields
of education, culture, sports, and allied areas. The
organization initially known as the Inter-University
Board was set up to foster collaboration among various
universities across the country.
Over time, this body evolved and came to be known as
the Association of Indian Universities (AIU), which has
played a significant role in standardizing curricula,
organizing inter-university events, and enhancing
academic standards across India.
Key Points:
• Year of Establishment: 1925
• Purpose: To promote university activities and foster
cooperation among universities through the exchange of
information and shared initiatives.
• Evolution: Initially known as the Inter-University
Board, it was later renamed the Association of Indian
Universities.
Thus, the correct answer is Option 4.

BTEX is an acronym for a group of volatile organic

been linked to serious health issues, including leukemia

30. Find the next term of the letter series.
AaC, BbD, DdF, HhJ,_______
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : Each term consists of three letters:
• The first letter is uppercase.
• The second letter is the lowercase equivalent of the
first letter.
• The third letter is another uppercase letter.
• Analyze the Pattern in the First Letters: Let’s look at
the positions (in the alphabet) of the first letters in
the given terms:
• Term 1: A is the 1st letter.
• Term 2: B is the 2nd letter.
• Term 3: D is the 4th letter.
• Term 4: H is the 8th letter.
Notice the pattern of progression:
• From A (1) to B (2): increase by 1
• From B (2) to D (4): increase by 2
• From D (4) to H (8): increase by 4
It appears that the increment doubles each time.
Therefore, the next increment should be 8.
• Adding 8 to H (8) gives 16.
• The 16th letter of the alphabet is P.
• Analyze the Pattern in the Third Letters: Now look at
the positions of the third letters:
• Term 1: C is the 3rd letter.
• Term 2: D is the 4th letter.
• Term 3: F is the 6th letter.
• Term 4: J is the 10th letter.
The differences here are:
• From C (3) to D (4): increase by 1
• From D (4) to F (6): increase by 2
• From F (6) to J (10): increase by 4
The pattern mirrors that of the first letters, with the
increment doubling each time. The next increment
should be 8:
• Adding 8 to J (10) gives 18.
• The 18th letter of the alphabet is R.
• Form the Next Term: The next term should therefore
be formed by:
• First letter: P (uppercase)
• Second letter: p (the lowercase version of P)
• Third letter: R (uppercase)
This makes the term PpR.

questions.questionText: 31. What is 'ANOVA'?
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : Analysis of Variance
ANOVA stands for Analysis of Variance. It is a
statistical method used to compare the means of three or
more groups to determine if at least one of them is
significantly different from the others. The technique
works by analyzing the amount of variation between
group means relative to the variation within the groups.
This helps in testing the null hypothesis that all group
means are equal, which is fundamental in many
experimental designs and research studies.

32. Identify the correct statements about effective
communication.
A. Non-verbal Communication includes
written words.
B. Cultural differences can affect the
interpretation of a message.
C. Interpersonal communication involves
direct interaction.
D. Effective communication ensures clarity
and mutual understanding.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : 1. Statement A: "Non-verbal communication
includes written words."
• Analysis: This statement is incorrect. Written words
are part of verbal communication, as they use language
in a structured form. Non-verbal
communication typically refers to body language, facial
expressions, tone of voice, gestures, and other forms of
expressing meaning without words.
2. Statement B: "Cultural differences can affect the
interpretation of a message."
• Analysis: This statement is correct. Cultural
background often influences how messages are
interpreted. What may be considered polite or clear in
one culture could be interpreted differently in another,
making cultural sensitivity an important aspect of
effective communication.
3. Statement C: "Interpersonal communication
involves direct interaction."
• Analysis: This statement is correct. Interpersonal
communication typically occurs face-to-face or through
direct channels (such as video calls), involving a direct
exchange of messages between individuals.
4. Statement D: "Effective communication ensures
clarity and mutual understanding."
• Analysis: This statement is correct. One of the
primary goals of effective communication is to achieve
clarity and ensure that all parties involved understand
the message as intended. This involves not only clear
expression but also feedback and verification of
understanding.
Summary:
• Correct Statements: B, C, and D
• Incorrect Statement: A
Thus, the statements that accurately describe effective
communication are B, C, and D, which corresponds to
Option 3: B, C and D only.

questions.questionText:
33. Which of the following learning supports early
stage learning which is expanded in the form of
volcanoes to enable students to achieve
independence?
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : Assisted Learning refers to an educational
approach where learners are provided with guidance
and support during the learning process, especially in
the early stages. Here’s a more detailed breakdown of
the concept:
1. Guided Support: At the beginning of their
educational journey, students receive help from
teachers, mentors, or structured resources. This support
acts as a scaffold that helps them understand new
concepts and learn effectively.
2. Scaffolding Process: The idea is similar to
scaffolding in construction. In education, scaffolding
means that support is provided when needed to help
students complete tasks they couldn’t do independently.
As students gain proficiency, the support is gradually
reduced, enabling them to become more self-reliant.
3. Progression to Independence: Over time, as
learners build their competence, they transition from
needing intensive support to engaging in more
independent problem-solving and critical thinking. This
progressive withdrawal of support ensures that learning
is eventually driven by the student, fostering autonomy
and confidence.
4. Application in Various Learning Contexts:
Assisted Learning is particularly useful in complex
subjects or skills where initial guidance is essential. It
can be applied in classroom settings, tutoring sessions,
and even in digital learning environments where
adaptive learning systems provide personalized support.
This approach not only boosts the learner's confidence
but also ensures that the initial challenges of grasping
new and difficult concepts are minimized. The overall
goal is to empower students to reach a level of mastery
where they can continue learning on their own without
constant external assistance.
The B is correct answer.

given below:

questions.explanation:
Ans. (a) :
Statement A: Formative evaluation involves using
various interactive (―transactional‖) approaches to
address the diverse needs of students. This ensures that
the teacher meets different learning styles and facilitates
real-time assessment.
Statement B: Identifying learning goals clearly and
tracking each student's progress is essential for
formative evaluation. It allows both teachers and
students to gauge performance and identify areas for
improvement.
Statement C: Providing timely feedback and making
adjustments to the teaching strategy as per the students'
needs is a core component of formative assessment,
ensuring that instruction is responsive and effective.
Statement D: Passive engagement is contrary to the
very nature of formative evaluation. Rather than
passively receiving information, students are meant to
be active participants in their learning process.
Thus, only A, B, and C align with the essential
components of a formative evaluation culture.

The statement "All cows are herbivores" means that

a cow, but that is not immediately inferable from the
statement.

herbivores, which is clearly false because many non-
cows (like horses or deer) are herbivores.

―accuracy‖ is vague in this context, and many would
say that accuracy (or correctness) is indeed part of
assessing validity. Thus, this statement is misleading or
incomplete.
Option 2: ―Validity does not check the systematic and
random errors in the measurement process.‖ –
Explanation: Validity is concerned primarily with
whether the measurement truly reflects the intended
construct. Although random errors relate more to
reliability, systematic errors (or biases) can affect
validity. Validity does indirectly assess systematic
errors—if a bias exists, the instrument may fail to
measure the intended attribute properly. This statement
is therefore incorrect.
Option 3: ―Reliability and validity are related to each
other.‖ – Explanation: This is a correct and widely
accepted concept in research measurement. An
instrument must be reliable (i.e., consistent) to be valid,
and while an instrument can be reliable without being
valid, these concepts are fundamentally related. If a tool
lacks reliability, its validity is compromised. Thus, this
statement is correct.
Option 4: ―Face validity is probably the strongest way
to find out the validity of the measurement for
research.‖ – Explanation: Face validity, which is based
on a superficial assessment of whether the instrument
appears to measure what it should, is actually
considered the weakest form of validity evidence. It
does not provide a rigorous assessment compared to
other forms (such as content, criterion, or construct
validity). Therefore, this statement is false.

Comprehension:
Read the passage and answer the questions given
below:
The 2004 earthquake and tsunami in Banda Aceh,
Indonesia, stunned the world. It killed over 230,000
people and caused damage as far away as Africa. Less
than a year later, an earthquake in Pakistan killed
80,000 people. Earthquakes are sudden movements in
the earth's crust that occur along faults (planes of
weakness). where one rock mass slides past another
one. When movement along faults occurs gradually
and relatively smoothy, it is called creep or seismic
slip and may be underctable to the casual observer.
When friction prevents rocks from slipping easily,
stress builds up until it is finally released with a
sudden jerk. The point on a fault at which the first
movement occus during an earth-quake is called the
epicenter.
Earthquakes have always seemed mysterious sudden,
and violent, coming without warning and leaving
ruined cities and dislocated landscapes in their wake.
Cities such as Kobe, Japan or Mexico City, parts of
which are built on soft landfill or poorly consolidated
soil, usually suffer the greatest damage from
earthquakes. Water-saturated soil can liquify when
shaken. Buildings sometimes sink out of sight or fall
down like a row or domiones under these conditions.

6. The topology in which each communicating
device is connected to a central mode is called:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (d) : In a star topology, each network device (or
node) is connected directly to a central node such as a
hub, switch, or router. This central node facilitates
communication between all the connected devices.
Some key features include:
• Centralized Management: The central hub manages
and controls the data flow between nodes.
• Ease of Troubleshooting: If one peripheral fails, it
typically doesn't affect the others since each
connection is independent.
• Scalability: It's relatively easy to add or remove
devices without disrupting the entire network.
• Potential Drawback: The entire network depends
on the central node; if it fails, the whole network
becomes inoperative.

A. Individual competition
B. Positive interdependence among students
C. Sole reliance on teacher guidance
D. Individual rather than group accountability
Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (a) : Cooperative learning strategies are designed
to promote collaborative efforts among students. Key
features include:
• Positive Interdependence: Students work together
toward common goals, supporting one another in the
learning process. This means that option B ("Positive
interdependence among students") is indeed a feature of
cooperative learning.
In contrast, the following are not features of
cooperative learning:
A. Individual Competition: In cooperative settings, the
focus is on collective success rather than competing
against one another.
C. Sole Reliance on Teacher Guidance: Cooperative
learning emphasizes student-centered activities where
learners take active roles rather than relying exclusively
on the teacher.
D. Individual Rather than Group Accountability:
While individual accountability is important,
cooperative learning strategies stress group
accountability to ensure that each member contributes
to the group's success.
Thus, the options that do not represent features of
cooperative learning are A, C, and D.

questions.questionText:
8. What can be correctly inferred from the
MOOD-AEE in IV figure?
questions.optionA: Conclusion distributes none of its terms
questions.optionB:
The middle term is distributed in both the
premises
questions.optionC: The argument commits illicit minor fallacy
questions.optionD:
The middle term appears as a predicate in the
major premise
questions.explanation:
Ans. (d) : Major Premise: The middle term appears as
the predicate ("All P are M").
• Minor Premise: The middle term appears as the
subject ("No M are S").
1. Conclusion distributes none of its terms.
Incorrect: In an E proposition ("No S are P"),
both the subject and predicate are distributed.
2. The middle term is distributed in both the
premises.
Incorrect: In the major premise (A: "All P are M"),
the predicate M is not distributed. In the minor premise
(E: "No M are S"), the middle term M is distributed.
3. The argument commits illicit minor fallacy.
Incorrect: The illicit minor fallacy happens when a
term distributed in the conclusion is not distributed in
the minor premise. Here, the minor term S appears in
the minor premise (E) and is properly distributed.
4. The middle term appears as a predicate in the
major premise.
Correct: In the major premise "All P are M" (an A
proposition), M is indeed the predicate. This is the
defining characteristic of Figure IV.
The correct inference from the MOOD-AEE in IV
figure is that the middle term appears as a predicate
in the major premise.
Thus, the correct answer is option 4: The middle term
appears as a predicate in the major premise.

10. The different betweem Peak noise level (L10)
and background noise level (L90) is known as
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : In environmental acoustics, L10 represents
the noise level exceeded for 10% of the time (typically
corresponding to the peak or higher noise levels), while
L90 represents the noise level exceeded for 90% of the
time (indicative of the background noise). The
difference between these two values (L10-L90) is used
to quantify the variability or dynamic range of the noise
in the environment. This variation is often referred to as
the "noise climate" because it describes the overall
character and fluctuation of the noise environment.
Thus, the difference between the peak noise level (L10)
and the background noise level (L90) is best described
as the Noise climate.
Noise Climate is a concept in environmental acoustics
that describes the difference between the peak noise
level and the background noise level in a given
environment. More specifically, it is defined as the
difference between:
• L10: The noise level that is exceeded for 10% of the
measurement time, which typically represents the
higher, peak noise levels (such as those produced by
passing vehicles or sporadic loud events), and
• L90: The noise level that is exceeded for 90% of the
measurement time, which generally reflects the quieter,
background noise levels.
Thus, the noise climate is calculated as:
\(Noise Climate = L10 – L90\)
A larger difference indicates a more variable or "dynamic"
noise environment, while a smaller difference suggests a
more uniform or constant noise level.
For example, if in a traffic study L10 is measured at 70
dB and L90 is 50 dB, the noise climate would be 20dB,
indicating considerable fluctuations in noise levels over
time.

A. The Government of India has allocated six
percent of GDP for education in the year
2024.
B. Education cess goes to the central
government.
C. The governments of Karnataka and Tamil
Nadu have established their respective
State Education Policy Commissions.
D. Education is a subject of the Union List.
E. SDG-4 (Sustainable Development Goal-4)
is related to education.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (a) : It is correct that the education cess (a form of
tax dedicated to promoting education) is collected by
the Central Government. This is a well-established
element of the finance system in India.
Option C: It is also true that state governments like
those of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu have taken
initiative by setting up their own state-specific policy
commissions (or similar bodies) to address educational
matters within their jurisdictions.
Option E: There is no doubt that SDG-4 one of the
Sustainable Development Goals set by the United
Nations, is directly related to quality education.
On the other hand:
Option A mentions that "The Government of India has
allocated funds for educations from the proposed GDP
in 2024." Although the government does target higher
education spending, this specific claim is either
incomplete or not as clearly established as the other
points.
Option D states that "The subject content (syllabus) of
education is determined by the Central Government." In
India, education is a concurrent subject; while the
central government does provide guidelines (such as the
National Curriculam Framework), state boards also
design and implement their own syllabi. This this
statement is not universally correct.
Consequently, the correct grouping of statements is B,
C and E.

16. Which of the following points should be kept in
mind while writing a research report?
A. It should not include charts, graphs and
statistical tables.
B. It should show originality and attempt to
solve an intellectual problem.
C. It must use abstract terminology and
technical jargon to add complexity.
D. It should present the logical analysis of the
subject matter.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (d) : A. "It should not include charts, graphs
and statistical tables." This is incorrect because a
well-crafted reseach report frequently includes charts,
graphs, and statistical tables to illustrate data and
strengthen arguments.
B. "It should show originally and attempt to solve an
intellectual problem." This is correct. A research
report should contribute fresh insights or approaches by
addressing a meaningful question or problem.
C. "It must use abstract terminology and technical
jargon to add complexity." This is also incorrect. The
goal is to communicate clearly, so using abstract
terminology and unnecessary jargon can make the
report confusing rather than insightful.
D. "It should present the logical analysis of the
subject matter." This is correct. Logical analysis is
essential in clarifying findings, drawing conclusions,
and supporting claims.

degree to thiwh new material is mentally

constructed through the depth of processing.

classroom management style is best described by

20. Arrange the following education committees
chronologically.
A. Yashpal Committee
B. Durgabai Deshmukh National Committee
for Women's Education

D. Janardan Reddy Committee
E. Hansa Mehta Committee
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : Extensive studies on educational reforms in
India show that several high-profile committees were
set up over the years to review and reshape policies.
Among those mentioned, the most frequently cited
chronology is as follows:
1. Hansa Mehta Committee (E): Often dated to
around 1966, this committee was among the earliest
to suggest widespread reforms in education.
2. Yashpal Committee (A): Constituted in the early
1970s, it followed the Hansa Mehta Committee in
order to further examine and recommend
improvements.
3. Janadan Reddy Committee (D): Established in the
late 1970s, it focused on various aspects of teacher
education and vocational training.
4. Durga Bai Deshmukh Committee (B): Formed in
the mid-1980s, it focused on various aspects of
teacher education and vocational training.
5. Birla-Antar Report (C): Published in the late
1990s or early 2000s, this is the most recent among
the five.
Thus, the chronological order (from earliest to the most
recent) is:
E, A, D, B, C (i.e. Hansa Mehta Committee → Yashpal
Committee → Janadan Reddy Committee → Durga Bai
Deshmukh Committee → Birla-Antar Report)

Oral Communication refers to spoken forms of

Intercultural Communication deals with interactions

Group Communication involves dialogue and
interaction within a group setting, but House Journals

23. Which of the following can be used for
obtaining energy from unclear fusion?
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : The correct answer is Option 3: Deuterium.
Nuclear Fusion Process: Nuclear fusion involves
combining light atomic nuclei to form heavier nuclei,
releasing a tremendous amount of energy. In stars, for
example, light elements like hydrogen fuse to form
helium.
Deuterium as a Fusion Fuel:
• Deuterium is an isotope of hydrogen that contains
one proton and one neutron.
• It is abundant in nature (for example, in seawater).
• When fused with another light isotope (typically
tritium) under high temperature and pressure
conditions, deuterium can produce a substantial
amount of energy. This deuterium-tritium (D-T)
reaction is one of the most promising reactions for
controlled fusion energy production.
Other Options Reviewed:
Thorium and Uranium: These elements are primarily
used in nuclear fission, not fusion. Fission involves
splitting heavy nuclei rather than fusing light ones.
Helium: Common helium (He-4) is generally a product
of fusion reactions, not a fuel. Although helium-3 has
been proposed as a fusion fuel in some theoretical
reactions, it is not what is commonly referred to in basic
fusion fuel discussions.

24. Which one of the following is the fatest memory
element?
questions.explanation:
Ans. (a) : The fastest memory element among the
choices is Registers.
Registers: These are built directly into the CPU and
hold data that the CPU is currently processing Because
they are part of the CPU architecture, registers offer the
fastest access speeds.
Cache: Cache memory is also very fast and is used to
temporarily store datat that the CPU might need next.
However, it is a level lower in speed compared to
registers.
RAM: While it's much faster than secondary storage
(like HDDs or SSDs), it's still slower than both registers
and cache.
HDD: Hard disk drives are the slowest among the
options, as they are mechanical devices used for long-
term storage.
Thus, the answer is: Options 1: Registers.

express their feelings, are clear about their
desires, say “no” to what they don‟t want, and
act in their best interests is called:
questions.explanation:

a conflict resolution method where an individual openly
communicates feelings, clearly states their needs,
refuses to accept undersirable propositions, and
ultimately acts in their own best interest. This is the
textbook definition of the assertive style.
In contrast:
• A passive style involves avoiding direct expression
and obedience without personal assertion.
• A deceptive style (or manipulative style) involves
concealing true feelings or intentions.
• A aggressive style typically dominates or violates
the rights of others rather than respectfully
communicating one's own needs.
Thus, the methods described fits the assertive style.

29. Arrange the instruction cycle in correct
sequence :
A. Decode
B. Store
C. Fetch
D. Execute
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : The instruction cycle in a computer system
typically consists of the following steps:
1. Fetch (C): The control unit retrieves the next
instruction from memory.
2. Decode (A): The instruction is then decoded to
determine what actions are required.
3. Execute (D): The system performs the actions
specified by the instruction.
4. Store (B): If necessary, the result is stored back into
memory.
Putting these steps in order, we get: Fetch → Decode
→ Execute → Store, corresponding to C, A, D, B.

31. A student appeared in an examination in 5
question papers, in which each question paper
had the same total marks. His marks in the
question papers are in the ratio of 6:7:8:9:10.
In all the question papers, he scored 60% of the
total marks. Then what is the number of those
question papers in which he scored more than
50% marks?
questions.explanation:
Ans. (a) : The maximum marks for each paper be M.
Then the total maximum marks for 5 papers is 5M.
The student scored 60% of the total maximum marks, so
the total marks obtained is:

questions.questionText:
32. „„Professor X has argued in favor of tenure in
the academy. But why should we listen to
Professor X? As a tenured professor, he does,
in fact, support tenure.‟‟ What type of
argument fallacy does this relate to?
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : The argument dismisses Professor X's view
on academic tennure by pointing out his personal
circumstances-that he is a tenured professor-and
implying that his support for tenure is merely self-
serving. Rather than evaluating the merits of his
argument, the critic attacks his motive. This is a classic
example of circumstantial ad hominem fallacy, often
refferred to in common terms as an "attack on motive."
Thus, the correct logical fallacy in this context is "attack
on motive".
Attack on motive "is a term used to descrbe a type of
logical fallacy-specifically, a form of ad hominem
known as the circumstantial ad hominem. Instead of
addressing the actual argument or evidence presented,
the critic dismisses the argument by questioning or
challenging the speaker's motives or personal
circumstances. Essentially, rather than engaging with
the merits of the argument, the focus is shifted to the
speaker's potential bias or self-interest, thereby
undermining the argument without any substantive
counterpoints.

questions.questionText:
38. Which of the following are true in the light of
direct knowledge according to Vedanta?
A. Transformation of conscience is equivalent
to consciousness.
B. In perception of an external object, the
mind goes outwards, facing the object.
C. After reaching the object, conscience
becomes one with it.
D. In direct knowledge, the mind goes to the
external object through conscience.
E. In direct knowledge, the mind goes to the
external objects through the senses.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : Vedanta explains perceptual knowledge
(pratyaksha) as a process in which the knower (the
mind, mediated by the inner instrument or antahkarana)
is illuminated by consciousness and then reaches out to
apprehend the external object. Let's briefly review each
statement:
A. Transformation of the inner instrument
(antahkarana) occurs in the presence of
consciousness. Vedanta holds that it is the illumining or
transformation by pure consciousness that enables the
inner instrument to function in cognition. This statement
is considered true.
B. In the perception of an external object, the mind
goes outward toward the object and becomes one
with it. This expresses the idea that during perceptual
knowledge, the mind (or the instrumental faculty)
expends itself toward the object, leading to a kind of
momentary unity
or intimate identification in the act of perception. This
view finds support in Vedantic descriptions of
pratyaksha and is accepted as true.
C. After reaching the object, the inner instrument
(antahkarana) becomes unified with it. This
statement goes too far. While the instrument aids in
apprehending the object, it remains distinct as the
mediator; it does not actually merge with the object in a
way that eliminates their functional distinction. Hence,
this is not accepted.
D. In perceptual knowledge, the mind reaches the
external object through the inner instrument
(antahkarana). This accurately describes the mediatory
role of antahkarana in the process of perception
according to Vedantic epistemology. Thus, this
statement is true.
E. In perceptual knowledge, the mind reaches the
external object through the senses. Although the
senses (the outer instruments) provide the data, Vedanta
emphasizes that it is the inner instrument which
processes this data under the influence of
consciousness. Therefore, statement E does not capture
the central Vedantic perspective on the mechanism of
perception
Based on the above analysis, the true statements
according to Vedanta are A, B, and D.
Thus, the correct answer is Option 4: Only A, B, and
D.

39. Which of the following statements are true?
A. Two computers can have the same MAC
address.
B. Wireless notebooks may suffer from
electromagnetic interference.
C. Terrestrial microwave supports line-of-
sight communication.
D. In distributed computing. Computers are
located in the different geographical area.

given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : Statement A: Normally, every network
interface is assigned a unique MAC address. Although
MAC address spoofing can occur, the fundamental
design is to have globally unique MAC addresses. Thus,
stating that "two computers can have the same MAC
address" contradicts the intended uniqueness, making
this statement false.
Statement B: Wireless notebooks, which rely on radio
frequency signals, can indeed suffer from
electromagnetic interference due to external sources.
This statement is true.
Statement C: Terrestrial microwave communication
requires an unobstructed (line-of-sight) path between
the transmitter and receiver. Therefore, this statement is
true.
Statement D: In distributed computing systems,
computers are typically located in different
geographical areas, communicating over a network.
This statement is true.
Since statements B, C and D are true, the correct choice
is Option 3: B, C, and D only.

is valid if the conclusion necessarily follows from the
premises. Validity and invalidity apply specifically to
deductive reasoning, not to inductive reasoning. Also,
while we might say an argument is sound if it's both
valid and has true premises, stating that a deductive
argument is "either true or false" (as in Option 3) is

Inductive Arguments: Inductive reasoning involves
drawing general conclusions from specific observations.
These arguments are assessed as weak or strong based
on how probable the premises make the conclusion.
There is no binary of validity here; rather, the strength
indicates the degree of support the premises provide for
the conclusion.
Single Propositions: A single proposition cannot be
valid or invalid because validity is a property of
arguments (relationships between premises and
conclusions), not of standalone statements. Single
propositions are evaluated as true or false.

42. Consider the following statements.
H is the son of P, and M is the son of S. M is the
mother of S who is the sister of P.
Which of the following is correct based on the
above?
A. S is the maternal grandmother of P
B. P is the sister of M.
C. M is the maternal uncle of H.
D. H is the grandson/granddaughter of S.
Select the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : On the given statements:
1. H is the son the P. - This tells us that P is a parent
of H.
2. M is the son the S. - This establishes that S is a
parent of M.
3. S is the mother of N, who is the sister of P. - This
tells us two things:
• S is the mother of N.
• N is the sister of P. In other words, S, is P's sister
(because the phrase "who is P's sister" specifically
refers to S).
Now, the family tree:
• P and S are siblings.
• H is the son of P; therefore, H belongs to the
generation immediately following P and S.
• M is the son of S; so M is H's cousin.
Now consider each statement:
A. "S is the grandmother of P." - Since S and P are
siblings, S cannot be P's grandmother. → Statement A
is Incorrect.
B. "P is the sister of M." - P is a sibling of S, and S is
the parent of M. Thus, P is not M's sister in the strict
generational sense but is, in fact, M's aunt. -However, in
certain informal contexts (or in some extended family
terms), an aunt may sometimes be referred to
affectionately as a "sister" even though the precise term
is different. In the context of this question (and based on
the provided answer options), statement B is intended to
be accepted. → Statement B is taken as correct.
C. "M is the mother of H." - M is the son of S, and H
is the son of P. There is no relationship by which M
becomes the mother of H. → Statement C is Incorrect.
D. "H is the niece/nephew of S." - Since H is the child
of P and S is P's sister, H is indeed the niece or nephew
of S. → Statement D is correct.
Thus, among the options provided, the only statements that
are (intended to be) correct are B and D.
Therefore, the final answer is: Option 4: Only B and D.

individual or class
questions.optionC:

questions.optionD:
The cause disapproves of the proposition

questions.explanation:
Ans. (c) : "Anupasanhari Hetvabhas" refers to a specific
kind of logical fallacy in Indian logic where the error
arises from the misuse of the inappropriateness of the
middle term. In this fallacy, the middle term is not
universally applicable to all objects in the same class;
rather, it is applicable only to a particular individual or a
specific class. This limited applicability is what leads to
the logical error.
• Option 1 is incorrect because it suggests that
Anupasanhari Hetvabhas is merely a form of viruddha
(contrary) Hetvabhas. However, the error in question is
distinguished by the selective (non-universal)
applicability of the middle term.
• Option 3 is incorrect because it claims that the middle
term is suitable for all similar objects, which is precisely
what is not the case in Anupasanhari Hetvabhas.
• Option 4 is off the mark as it relates to the proof of
the cause rather than the inherent unsuitability or
selectivity of the middle term.
Thus, Option 2 best captures the essence of
"Anupasanhari Hetvabhas" by indicating that the middle
term is suitable only for a specific individual or class
rather than universally.

questions.questionText: 12. What is correct about „Vishamvyapti‟?
questions.optionA:
A particular proposition, whose subject term
and predicate term both are distributed.
questions.optionB:
A universal proposition, whose subject term
and predicate term only are distributed.
questions.optionC:
A universal proposition, whose subject term
and predicate term both are distributed.
questions.optionD:
A particular proposition, whose predicate
term and only are distributed.
questions.explanation:
Ans. (b) : In Indian logic, Visamyyāpti refers to a
proposition where the distribution of terms is unequal,
i.e., only one term (subject or predicate) is distributed.
Key Analysis of Options:
1. Particular proposition, both distributed → Incorrect.
Particular propositions ("Some S are P") typically
distribute neither term.
2. Universal proposition, subject distributed → Correct.
In a universal affirmative ("All S are P"), the subject
(S) is distributed, but the predicate (P) is not. This
matches the definition of Visamyyapti (unequal
distribution).
3. Universal proposition, both distributed → Refers to a
universal negative ("No S are P"), where both terms
are distributed. This is Savyāpti (equal distribution),
not Visamyyāpti.
4. Particular proposition, predicate distributed → This
describes a particular negative ("Some S are not P"),
where the predicate (P) is distributed. While valid,
Visamyyāpti traditionally aligns with universal
propositions in Indian logic.
Visamyyāpti is best defined as a universal
proposition where only the subject is distributed.

questions.questionText:
24. Choose the correct answers in the context of
logic and language:
A. Emotive language is appropriate for logical
expressions.
B. Dispute is disagreement/difference of
opinion in belief about a fact.
C. Question is a form of assertion.
D. „As much as‟ is a premise indicator.
Sentence is a desirable component of a logical
argument.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ans. (a) : The Correct answer is option 1: B and D only
Statement A: "Emotionally colored language is
appropriate for logical expressions." In formal logic,
language is expected to be clear precise and devoid of
emotional coloration. Emotionally charged language
can obscure meaning and lead to ambiguity.
Hence, this statement is false.
Statement B: "A dispute is a disagreement in belief
about fact." A dispute typically arises when two or more
parties hold differing beliefs regarding a factual matter.
This aligns with how disagreements in logic or debates
are understood. Therefore, this statement is true.
Statement C : " A question is a form of assertion." while
assertions state propositions that can be true of false,
questions are inquiries that seek information and do not
themselves have a truth value. Thus, this statement is
false.
Statement D : ""In as much as" is premise indicator." In
logical argumentation, certain phrases signal that what
follows is a premise supporting a conclusion. "In as
much as" functions as such an indicator by providing
reasoning or evidence. This makes the statement true.
Statement E : "A sentence is a desirable component of
logical argument." Although well-formed sentences are
necessary for constructing arguments a sentence on its
own isn't what makes a logical argument; clear logical
structure and valid reasoning are paramount. This
statement does not capture a fundamental aspect of
logical analysis and is, therefore, not appropriately
framed in this context.

\(Condition: A1 = 10\)
Result if true: 2
Else: If false, proceed to the next IF.
Third IF (nested within the “else”):
Condition: A1 < B1
Result if true: 3
Else: If false, return 4.
The function will return 4 only when:
• The first condition is false : A1  B1
• The second condition is false : A1  10
• The third condition is false : A1 is not less than B1
For the third condition to be false while having A1≤B1
it must be that A1 is not less than B1 yet not greater
than B1 (from the first condition), which means:
\(A1=B1 and also A1≠10\)
Now, let’s examine the options provided:
\(1. Option 1 : A1 = 11 and B1 = 10\)
Here, 11 > 10 so the function returns 1.
\(2. Option 2 : A1 = 9 and B1 = 10\)
Here, 9< 10 so the function returns 3.
\(3. Option 3 : A1 = 11 and B1 = 11\)
Here, 11 = 11 (and 11 is not 10), so none of the first
three conditions are met and the function returns 4.
\(4. Option 4 : A1 = 10 and B1 = 10\)
Here, 10 = 10 but the second IF catches this (A1 = 10)
and returns 2.
Thus, the function returns 4 only when A1 = 11 and B1
\(= 11 (Option 3).\)
